## Natural history notes

A medium-sized owlet moth characterized by mottled brown, gray, and tan forewings with jagged crosslines and a bark-like pattern that helps it blend against tree trunks and dead leaves. In Florida, it is found in wooded and semi-wooded habitats such as hammocks, pine-oak woods, forest edges, parks, and yards where suitable hardwood host plants occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on tree and shrub foliage and help transfer plant material into the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
